findings.reason: adding `s4` to `s3`'s depends-on is what sends the node at the rule it must consume instead of re-deriving it, and without it the quarter lands a second copy of the retention rule.
findings.text: §3's done-when requires the served listing to return an unreferenced report as `working` with its expiry date and a cited path as `cited`, which are §4's keep-and-expiry rule; §3 declares `depends-on` `s2` only (line 24) and only §5 waits for both. A node building §3 alone must either duplicate §4's rule inside the listing payload — two implementations of one truth, which this repo's AGENTS.md forbids — or invent a placeholder expiry §4 then has to reconcile.

findings.reason: naming a negative control (a deliberately non-settled folder that must appear as kept) is what turns the log into evidence that the predicate ran, and this node is the one that moves 330 GB.
findings.text: §6's entire guard is the "settled" predicate (unchanged 7 days, fresh comparison lists no difference, counts and bytes match) that decides whether a folder is linked to `/work` or kept on home, yet its done-when asks only that the log names every child folder as linked or kept with a reason, plus `du` before and after. A node whose settle check always answers "settled" links all of imas-efit's and nova's child folders and satisfies both measures; nothing states a folder that must be kept, so the guard's firing is never observed.

findings.reason: the plan must state whether a citation of any path inside an item keeps the item, because the two readings differ only in production, where one of them deletes the figures plans cite.
findings.text: §4 defines an item as a child folder of a project's reports directory (a run folder such as `reports/reckon/a-held-dispatch-waits-its-fair-turn` or a plan-review run directory) but its keep rule is "its path appears in a plan, research or evidence document". A plan cites a path inside that folder, never the folder path, so the rule as written expires exactly the cited run folders it exists to protect; an implementer reading it literally will prefix-match nothing and delete cited evidence, while one writing the test as "cite the folder path itself" passes and never reveals the difference.
